issues.text: Д14 is built as FX3 was measured, with two completions of the same G1 kind (AP-014). (a) The scanned boxes include the body, which FX3 stops below. (b) The window itself counts as a box: if it scrolled vertically and its overflow is hidden or clip, the check fails. The window's overflow is the root's, or the body's when the root's is visible, as CSS hands it to the window. Measured: TF3, TF3b and TF3c are green with the gate's FX3 (X3a-X3c) and red with this form. The benign twin TF3g (the root's vertical overflow scroll) and TF2v (a plain page scroll) are green, quiet and loaded. Both completions stay inside Д14's own words ('any box the person cannot scroll'). The single boolean also became five named parts, so a red names what failed, as the task asks.

The ways I still see to defeat the check, for ORCH and the last gate. Three are measured green on this form; none is one of Д14's conditions. (1) A button that is not painted: opacity 0 on it or an ancestor (TF4 green), or transparent colours or a colour equal to the background. The hit test reads elements, not pixels. (2) An opaque box over the button with pointer-events: none (TF5 green). elementFromPoint skips it, so the person can click through but cannot see the button. (3) A button made tiny: a transform to 2 percent (TF6 green). Its rectangle is above 0 and the centre is still the button. (4) One point only: a box or a clip-path that hides all of the button but its centre passes (not measured). (5) 'Can scroll' is read from the computed style: an auto box that the person's wheel or keys cannot reach (pointer-events: none, no scrollbar) still counts as scrollable (not measured). (6) One moment: the check reads once, right after the list loads. A page that hides or moves the button later is not seen (AP-159 (5) kind), and only the three named window sizes are read. (7) The page's realm: REACH runs as page code. A page that replaces scrollIntoView, getBoundingClientRect, getComputedStyle or elementFromPoint can make any reading. Closing (1)-(4) and (7) needs an oracle outside the page, for example a real click through the browser protocol at the button's centre that must submit the form, or a screenshot of the button's rectangle against the page without it. Closing (3) and (1) also needs a threshold (a minimum size or contrast), which is a decision. Each is a new decision or a new defect, not this step (AP-019).

One assertion is replaced and none is dropped. The single assert.equal(await page.evaluate(INSIDE), true, '<w>: the create button is inside the window') becomes a loop of assert.equal(reach?.[part], true, '<w>: the create button <part>') over five parts. Every condition of the old boolean is in a part: s.left and s.right in 'sideways', scrollX in 'noSidewaysScroll', the rectangle after the scroll in 'inWindow' (it keeps the old message). The new conditions are 'noHiddenScroll' and 'atCentre'. The textual count of assert. stays 113, the same as at step 7b; at run time each window now asserts 5 parts where it asserted 1.

For DOC-UPDATER (AP-143), counted on tools/test/e2e/team-web.e2e.js. grep -c '^test(' gives 7. grep -o 'assert\.' | wc -l gives 113 (108 on the tag, 112 at step 6, 113 at steps 7b and 7d). wc -l gives 1584. The sha256 is 61d69de84552cd5de36ab629a990ff800cdd9a734dc206241a9923a73c58090a. The way back (role file, item 8): a test edit goes to TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (step 7e, the last pass, Д16).
